assumptions: the pinned census roots are treated as the five declared local root centers; this calculation does not claim an exhaustive root classification outside its fixed prior census
the generalized fiber equation is L_p u=lambda f u with the declared Gamma_1,p=0 boundary line and plus-end solution continuation
the Wronskian/Lagrange identity includes the p-dependent boundary-domain contribution through F_lambda and is the declared route to the local slope

the runner does not construct a nonzero-lambda plus-end Weyl solution or independently finite-difference F_lambda; every reported lambda slope and delta(C) Jacobian is conditional on the stated moving-boundary Lagrange identity and its hypotheses
N_f is positive for a nonzero real u_0 and finite because the f-weight becomes a z^(1/2) Mellin integrand
the optional bounded log-z quadrature is an independent numerical cross-check of the Mellin formula, not a replacement for endpoint/domain analysis

the naive fixed-domain Hellmann-Feynman expression based on integral |u_0|^2 dQ is not used: it diverges at the limit-circle minus end for K_(i*kappa), and it omits the p-dependent boundary-domain contribution

declared_conventions.p_branch: p>0 for reported lambda_prime; p<0 has the opposite slope because the declared spectrum is even in p

exact_calculation.conditionality: F_lambda, lambda_prime and the local Jacobian are conditional on the moving-boundary Lagrange theorem guard; this runner does not solve or finite-difference the nonzero-lambda Weyl problem

exact_checks.statement: at hbar=1, f(Q)dQ=(sqrt(2/3)/pi) z^(1/2)dz under z=6*pi^2e^Q
each pinned root has nonzero F_kappa and is locally simple in the declared characteristic variable
each a=K_(i*kappa)(z_0) is nonzero, so the declared F_lambda division is defined
each declared weighted Mellin norm is positive and nonzero
each moving-domain characteristic derivative F_lambda is nonzero
each positive-p local eigenvalue slope is nonzero
F_lambda has sign opposite a, and the negative-p branch has exactly the opposite local slope

numerical_calculation.conditionality: reported F_lambda, lambda_prime and local delta(C) Jacobians assume the declared moving-boundary Lagrange identity; no nonzero-lambda Weyl solve or direct F_lambda finite difference is performed
numerical_calculation.scope: five local simple-root controls and conditional local delta(C) Jacobians only; no global measure or RAQ

numerical_checks.statement: all evaluated real-kappa K quantities are real within the declared precision
five bounded log-z quadratures agree with the Mellin closed-form N_f values
centered F_kappa derivatives at steps h and h/2 agree before Richardson extrapolation

primary_sources.not_used_for: a full spectral theorem, raw-C rigging map, or C/H equivalence
primary_sources.source: I. S. Gradshteyn and I. M. Ryzhik, Table of Integrals, Series, and Products, 8th ed., formula 6.576(4)
primary_sources.used_for: the Mellin integral int_0^infinity x^(mu-1)K_nu(x)^2 dx used to normalize the declared weighted Lagrange identity

primary_sources.not_used_for: proving that this one raw-C extension is physically selected
primary_sources.source: T. Kato, Perturbation Theory for Linear Operators, Springer (1995 reprint)
primary_sources.used_for: the domain-dependence warning behind not applying a naive fixed-domain Hellmann-Feynman formula

primary_sources.not_used_for: positivity of a physical Hilbert product or observable action
primary_sources.source: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, modified Bessel functions, sections 10.25, 10.29 and 10.40
primary_sources.used_for: the zero-shell K_(i*kappa) convention and numerical evaluation of the characteristic derivative

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: F_lambda(0)=-N_f/(2*hbar^2*a); this supplies one local characteristic derivative only, not a global spectral theorem or rigging map
theorem_guards.hypotheses: u_0 is the declared plus-end zero-shell solution, a=u_0(Q_0) is nonzero at the pinned root, and F_lambda is the derivative of the characteristic boundary condition rather than a fixed-domain expectation value
theorem_guards.theorem: Lagrange identity for L_p u=lambda f u with a parameter-dependent self-adjoint boundary domain

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: N_f is finite and positive for each nonzero root under the declared normalization; this is not a physical inner-product positivity theorem
theorem_guards.hypotheses: mu=3/2 and nu=i*kappa with real kappa lie in the convergence range; the selected K solution is real on positive z

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: a naive fixed-domain Hellmann-Feynman formula is not used and cannot replace the Wronskian/Lagrange calculation
theorem_guards.hypotheses: K_(i*kappa)(z) has nondecaying oscillatory magnitude as Q tends to minus infinity, so integral |u_0|^2 dQ diverges; moreover the extension boundary data vary with p

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: 1/|lambda_prime| is a local Jacobian factor only; spectral normalization, test space, global summation and rigging-map data remain absent
theorem_guards.hypotheses: F_kappa and lambda_prime are nonzero at each pinned root and the statement is restricted to a local p branch
